subtitle: Economic nationalism, a new date, and a landslide.
objectives: Describe the Garcia and Macapagal administrations
Explain why Independence Day was moved to 12 June

cards.title: Economic nationalism, a new date, and a landslide
cards.text: The republic tried to take back economic control, then elected a man who promised to build.
cards.body: The republic tried to take back economic control, then elected a man who promised to build.

cards.title: 1957 to 1961: Filipino First
cards.text: He took over when Magsaysay died, then won his own term.
points: **Filipino First Policy** gave Filipino businesses priority.
**The aim** was to reduce foreign control of the economy.
**It annoyed American business interests.**
**It also drew accusations** of protecting the well-connected.

question.text: The Filipino First Policy aimed to…
options: give Filipino businesses priority in the economy
question.explain: Reducing foreign economic control was the point.

cards.title: 1961 to 1965: the date and the land code
points: **Moved Independence Day** from 4 July to 12 June, in 1962.
**The Agricultural Land Reform Code of 1963** attacked tenancy directly.
**It aimed to turn tenants into owners.**
**Funding and enforcement** fell far short.

cards.title: Changing a national holiday is an argument about history
cards.text: Moving the date said that independence was declared by Filipinos, not handed over by Americans.
points: **4 July 1946** was the day recognition was granted.
**12 June 1898** was the day it was declared.
**Macapagal chose the declaration.**
**Same country, two stories about where it begins.**

question.text: The 1963 land reform code ended tenancy in the Philippines.
question.explain: It aimed to, and fell far short on funding and enforcement. The problem continued.

cards.title: 1965 to 1972: build, borrow, win again
cards.text: He was elected on competence and a promise of infrastructure.
points: **Roads, bridges and schools** were built at pace.
**He borrowed heavily** to pay for them.
**Re-elected in 1969**, the first president to win a second full term.
**That campaign** was extraordinarily expensive.

question.text: Independence Day was moved to 12 June by…
question.explain: In 1962, to mark the declaration rather than the grant.

cards.title: Building on borrowed money
cards.text: Infrastructure you cannot pay for is a car bought on finance: real, useful, and still owed.
points: **The roads existed** and were genuinely used.
**So did the debt**, growing each year.
**Repayments** came out of later budgets.
**Both facts are true.** Hold them together.

cards.title: Unrest was rising before 1972
cards.text: Student protests, rural insurgency and a widening gap between rich and poor.
points: **The First Quarter Storm of 1970** saw mass student demonstrations.
**A new communist movement** had formed in 1968.
**A Muslim separatist movement** grew in Mindanao.
**All three were real** before martial law was declared.

terms.def: The wave of student protests in early 1970.
Roads, bridges, ports and public buildings.

cards.title: What to remember
points: Garcia's Filipino First tried to reduce foreign economic control.
Macapagal moved Independence Day to 12 June in 1962.
The 1963 land code aimed at tenancy and fell short.
Marcos built heavily, borrowed heavily, and won again in 1969.

teacher.summary: Term 2 Week 9 Social Studies, covering the administrations between Magsaysay and martial law. The week's purpose is to make 1972 intelligible rather than sudden, so the closing cards establish that student protest, a new communist movement and a Mindanao separatist movement were all real and growing before any declaration. Marcos before 1972 is presented accurately as a popular builder financed by debt, with both facts held together rather than one chosen. Macapagal's holiday change is used to show that choosing a national date is an argument about whether independence was declared or granted.
discussion: Why move Independence Day to 12 June?
Can infrastructure and debt both be real achievements and real problems?
extension: Find out what was built near you in the late 1960s.
Look up what the First Quarter Storm demanded.
misconceptions: That Marcos was unpopular before martial law.
